title: EmeraldCloud & Redwood - Partner Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and EmeraldCloud to evaluate partnership for reselling and joint go-to-market. Discussed EmeraldCloud's reseller model, technical constraints (VPC, HSM/KMS, multi-tenant isolation), interest in Dedicated and Private deployment options, benchmark requirements, and next steps for a pilot and NDA.
next_steps: Sofia to share partner integration guide and API contract link
Marcus to schedule technical deep dive and benchmark run for EmeraldCloud's test workloads
Alex to share projected volumes and customer use cases
Legal teams to exchange NDA and resell agreement draft
action_items: Sofia Patel - send integration guide and Redwood partner deck (due 2026-12-03)
Marcus Lee - prepare benchmark plan and propose test window (due 2026-12-07)
Alex Rivera - provide expected qps and monthly token estimates (due 2026-12-04)
Priya Nair - outline support/ops touchpoints for private deployments (due 2026-12-06)
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. we're from Redwood Inference — i'm Sofia, i'm the account lead. Marcus and Priya from our team are on -- Marcus is our solutions engineer and Priya runs partner eng. quick round-robin?
[00:12] Alex Rivera: Alex here, head of cloud partnerships at EmeraldCloud. Maya and Omar are with me.
[00:17] Maya Singh: hi all, Maya, director of solutions, I run integrations for platform partners.
[00:20] Omar Haddad: Omar, infra lead.
[00:22] Sofia Patel: great, thanks. agenda is fairly light: partner model discussion, technical constraints, what a pilot would look like, and next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Alex Rivera: yeah that works. quick context — EmeraldCloud is building a managed marketplace for GPU-backed infra, we resell partner inference stacks to our customers, and we're exploring Redwood as a partner to offer hosted and private options. main ask today is to see fit, technical fit and go-to-market flow.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: awesome. do you mind walking through Emerald's integration model? are you planning to resell hosted APIs under your brand, or run a co-managed private deployment in customers' VPCs?
[00:55] Maya Singh: primarily resell, but for strategic enterprise customers we do co-managed VPC deployments. We also have customers that require on-prem or air-gapped options.
[01:06] Marcus Lee: got it. on Redwood side we support three surfaces: hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). for reseller flows the hosted API is easiest — we can provide partner keys and usage tracking. for co-managed VPC we can do a private control plane and customer-managed networking.
[01:23] Omar Haddad: question — how do you handle KMS and HSM for customer-managed keys in the private deployment? security is the main blocker for some customers.
[01:32] Priya Nair: good question. Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS providers — AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and we have options for HSM through partner integrations. keys stay in the customer's account; Redwood doesn't persist plaintext keys. audit logs are forwarded to the customer's logging endpoint.
[01:48] Alex Rivera: that's helpful. on the reseller split, how do you handle rate limiting and multi-tenant isolation if multiple Emerald customers hit the hosted API via our keys? we need quotas per downstream tenant.
[02:00] Marcus Lee: we have token-level quotas and route-level policies. partners can create per-customer API keys and attach quotas and billing tags; we can do per-tenant rate limits and cost reporting in the console. For strict isolation, Dedicated pools per tenant are possible but that's more of a commercial commitment.
[02:18] Maya Singh: latency and cost tradeoffs are important — many of our customers care about sub-100ms token latency for chat workloads. can you give a sense of latency profiles across model sizes?
[02:29] Marcus Lee: sure, rough numbers — small Llama variants 7B in optimized quantized mode can hit 30-80ms tail for single-token on modern A100 class hardware with our continuous batching disabled; 13B/30B will be higher. Redwood has smart routing so we can route by latency SLO to lower-cost variants. our published benchmarks vary by sequence length, so we'd run your workloads for accurate numbers.
[02:48] Omar Haddad: do you support KV cache sharing or cross-request caching for few-shot workloads to reduce cost?
[02:53] Priya Nair: yes — prefix and KV caching is supported in the runtime, and partners can configure cache TTLs. that often reduces token costs significantly for repeated prompts.
[03:03] Alex Rivera: on pilot scope: we want a sandbox where we can emulate two of our customers — one high-volume chat and one embedding-heavy search use case. what would you need to run a benchmark?
[03:12] Marcus Lee: sample prompt sets, token length distributions, concurrency profile (qps), and a few representative input sizes. ideally an anonymized sample of workload. we can run a 48-72 hour benchmark across hosted and dedicated configurations.
[03:25] Maya Singh: would you run the benchmark in your hosted environment or can we have it run within our VPC to test private latency?
[03:32] Marcus Lee: both are possible — hosted is fastest to spin up. for VPC-private benchmarks, we ask for network peering details and permit list. the test in VPC helps validate egress and cold-start behavior.
[03:43] Alex Rivera: ok. on compliance — SOC 2 and ISO are core to enterprise customers, also SAML SSO and RBAC. can you surface audit logs per-customer?
[03:53] Priya Nair: we ship audit logs and integrate with SIEMs; role-based access control and SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported. SOC 2 Type II attestation is available; we can share the compliance pack.
[04:04] Omar Haddad: what about data residency? some customers want EU-only storage and log retention.
[04:10] Sofia Patel: we can route requests regionally and keep logs in specific regions for enterprise accounts, that would typically be part of the Private or Dedicated offering with contract terms.
[04:19] Maya Singh: commercial — what's the partner margin or reseller pricing? are you comfortable with a margin for EmeraldCloud and also offering a referral fee?
[04:27] Sofia Patel: we have partner pricing tiers and reseller agreements; can follow up with specifics. typically partners get discounted committed rates for resell plus an additional referral or marketplace fee; we'll share a partner pricing sheet after legal sync.
[04:39] Alex Rivera: perfect. competitors — we've evaluated Lambda and Paperspace; some customers evaluated NVIDIA DGX Cloud. how does Redwood position vs those?
[04:47] Marcus Lee: we focus on production-grade inference and operational tooling — batching, KV cache, smart routing, and observability. many infra vendors run hardware; Redwood offers the serving runtime and orchestration to sit on top. for deeper HW partnerships we often work with GPU vendors for optimizations.
[05:02] Maya Singh: tiny nit — earlier you said Redwood Dedicated, i heard "Redwood Dedicate" on the doc.
[05:06] [laughter]
[05:08] Sofia Patel: noted, transcription quirk.
[05:10] Alex Rivera: any known hard limits we should be aware of? like max tokens per request, concurrency per key?
[05:16] Marcus Lee: defaults are configurable. we typically support large request sizes up to model limits, and concurrency depends on pool sizing. for pilot we'll recommend target qps and concurrency with autoscaling policies.
[05:27] Maya Singh: for the pilot timeline, EmeraldCloud would like to run an initial 4-week sandbox and then a 90-day co-sell pilot for 2-3 enterprise customers. is that feasible?
[05:36] Sofia Patel: yes that aligns with standard partner pilots. initial sandbox 2-4 weeks to validate integration, then a staged pilot with 2 customers. commercial paperwork usually takes a few weeks depending on legal.
[05:45] Omar Haddad: network — for VPC deployments do we need a particular CNI or k8s version, or is it more of a blackbox image?
[05:52] Priya Nair: for Redwood Private we provide Helm charts and a private control plane connector; we support mainstream k8s versions and common CNIs. if customers require air-gapped installs we have documented steps.
[06:04] Maya Singh: ok great. any blockers from your side to proceed to an NDA and pilot plan?
[06:09] Sofia Patel: no blockers. next steps: we'll send partner integration docs, compliance pack, partner pricing, and a proposed benchmark/test plan. Marcus will pick tentative dates for technical deep dive.
[06:21] Alex Rivera: i'll get volume estimates, sample prompts and legal contact for NDA.
[06:25] Sofia Patel: perfect. recapping action items...
[06:28] [00:06:28] Sofia Patel: Sofia to send docs and deck, Marcus to send bench plan, Alex to share volumes and legal contact. aim to have NDA signed and benchmark scheduled within two weeks.
[06:45] Maya Singh: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:48] Marcus Lee: thanks all.
[06:50] Alex Rivera: thanks.
[06:52] [call ends]
